label: prop:selection-rule-anchors-c1-c3
title: Per-component selection rule $\frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda$ at c=1, c=3
html:
Proposition. Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3

Let q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} and let h := q - q^{-1}. The per-component selection rule

  \mathrm{lw}(c)(q) \;:=\; \frac{1}{c+1} \sum_{\lambda \vdash (c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda

satisfies the two exact identities:

  \mathrm{lw}(1)(q) \;=\; 1 \qquad (\text{exactly, } \forall q > 0),
  \mathrm{lw}(3)(q) \;=\; \frac{3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2}}{4} \;=\; \frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4} h^2.

These form the muon (c=1, knot) and the proton (c=3, Borromean 3-link) anchors of the per-component selection rule.

Significance

The zero-parameter selection rule reads \mathrm{lw}(L) = \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash(c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda, where c is the number of link components. The c=1 case must equal 1 for all q (muon, a knot, framework linking_weight = 1). The c=3 case must equal the Family-A formula \frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4}h^2 (proton). This proposition Lean-formalises both identities from the hook-length formula itself: QOU.Mass.selection_rule_c1_real and QOU.Mass.selection_rule_c3_real state the sums over dimQ of the actual partitions, where dimQ is built as shape → conjugate → hook lengths → [n]_q! over the hooks' q-integers, and the hook multiset of each shape is settled by decide. So the anchors are derivation-tight in the sense claimed: not a fit, and not a hand-substituted value either.

What the earlier formalisation did and did not do. Until 2026-08-29 the Lean here proved ((1 : R) + 1) / 2 = 1 for c=1 and the corresponding Laurent identity for c=3 — true statements, but arithmetic over q-dimension values typed in by hand, with no partition, hook length or dim_q occurring in any statement. The hook-length step lived in a docstring. Those theorems remain in selection-rule-anchors-c1-c3.lean and are still true; what was missing, and is now supplied, is the derivation of their left-hand sides (bean qou-lx7k).

Lean proof structure

We provide two purely algebraic identities at the symbolic level, each closed by field_simp; ring:

  1. c=1 anchor (selection_rule_c1_eq_one): \frac{1}{2}\bigl( \dim_q V_{(2)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1)} \bigr) = 1. Both q-dimensions equal 1 (each partition of 2 has a hook product equal to the q-factorial), so the average is exactly 1.

  2. c=3 anchor (selection_rule_c3_eq_family_a): \frac{1}{4} \bigl( \dim_q V_{(4)} + \dim_q V_{(3,1)} + \dim_q V_{(2,2)} + \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} \bigr) = (3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2})/4.

    Using the explicit q-hook formula:

    • \dim_q V_{(4)} = \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} = 1
    • \dim_q V_{(3,1)} = \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} = [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}
    • \dim_q V_{(2,2)} = [4]_q / [2]_q = q^2 + q^{-2}

    Their sum is 1 + (q^2{+}1{+}q^{-2}) + (q^2{+}q^{-2}) + (q^2{+}1{+}q^{-2}) + 1 = 4 + 3q^2 + 3q^{-2}. Dividing by 4 yields the stated form. The h^2 form follows from q^2 + q^{-2} = h^2 + 2.

    Both steps operate as pure polynomial identities in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. They close by ring after field_simp clears the q^{-1} denominators.

q-usage discipline

This holds over real q > 0 (the substrate-anchor regime). Both identities are q-rational, fibre-level constructs. The c=1 case holds for ALL q > 0 (an infinite set of constraints, not a single point).
